messages:
marina: heads up — nightly perf showed a regression in v2 serving: p99 token latency up ~18% for chat workloads that rely on prefix reuse. noticed KV hit-rate drop from ~87% -> ~63% on the same replay. attaching the perfetto/heatmap link: https://perfetto.redwood.internal/trace/ABCD1234 :eyes:

aj: ugh. any obvious kernel fallbacks in the trace? or batching churn?

marina: opened an nsys capture (nvtx + sched + cuda) for the failing replay. timeline shows repeated short kernels that look like small GEMM launches instead of the fused attention kernel for many last-token steps. SM occupancy spikes then falls; there's a correlated increase in L2 miss rate. heatmap suggests reuse is fragmented across many prefixes.

ken: can you paste the nsys summary snippet? also which commit rolled last night?

marina: summary paste:
```
nsys profile --capture-range=nvtx --output=reg65
Total CUDA time: 1243ms
Top kernels:
 - aten_gemm_small (many launches, avg 0.9ms)
 - fused_attn_forward (fewer launches, avg 5.2ms)
Device L2 read bandwidth dip ~30% during small-launch phase
KV cache hit-rate per-prefix: heatmap shows diagonal broken into shards
```
Last deploy was 9f8c7b5 — that changes batching heuristics (batch policy: enable_reshuffle=true) and small change to prefix coalescer.

aj: that coalescer tweak could fragment prefixes so different requests miss shared cache. if batches are being reshuffled, similar prefixes might get split across micro-batches.

sylvie: confirming: the batch policy change toggles reshuffle when predicted latency > SLO. for short sequences it can reduce head-of-line waiting but might break prefix locality. we did unit tests but not full replay.

marina: right — reproduction steps I ran:
1) run replay harness with real chat traces (seq len mix 32/128/512)
2) enable new batchpolicy flag
3) capture nsys with `nsys profile -o /tmp/reg --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=nvtx`
observed: many small GEMM launches instead of single larger fused kernels at the same timesteps where KV hit-rate drops.

ken: hypothesis: reshuffle moves similar-prefix requests into different GPU contexts or micro-batches so our prefix coalescer no longer groups them; cache lookup pattern becomes random -> L2 eviction -> kernel selection heuristic thinks sequence is shorter and picks small-gemm path.

perf-bot: regression alert: p99 increased 18% on nightly, correlating commit 9f8c7b5. Adding label :regression:automated.

marina: quick check — I reverted the coalescer change locally and replayed: hit-rate returns to ~85% and p99 back to baseline. so looks like the coalescer/reshuffle interaction.

aj: good noisy test. can we add a small unit that ensures coalescer groups prefixes when reshuffle enabled? or update reshuffle to be prefix-aware?

sylvie: plan proposal:
 - rollback 9f8c7b5 to staging for now (blocking prod rollouts)
 - add a replay-based integ test that asserts KV-hit-rate >= 80% for the chat-replay suite when reshuffle=true
 - instrument the prefix coalescer with a histogram (per-batch prefix-entropy) and log to console for a few replays
 - run nsys with larger window (5 replays) and collect kernel selection stats to see transition thresholds

ken: also add targeted perfetto slices around kv lookup + kernel handoff. useful to see per-request latent gap between lookup and kernel launch.

marina: created rollback PR and test ticket: https://phabricator.redwood/r/PR-4123 — pushing traces and perfetto links to the ticket.

aj: one more thought: there might also be an NVTX labeling mismatch that made the profiler attribute fused_attn time to other regions when reshuffle changes ordering. please ensure NVTX scope names are stable across policy modes.

marina: noted — NVTX names invariant in my captures, but will double-check. also adding a small script to compute per-prefix reuse distance from logs.

deploy-bot: queued rollback to staging for change 9f8c7b5 — ETA 12m.

ken: awesome. once rollback is up, let's run the expanded replay + nsys capture and compare kernel histogram. if we still see anomalies, we dig into kernel selection code path (kernel_selector.cpp) for thresholding logic.

marina: thanks all — will follow up with perf dumps on the PR. TLDR: regression traced to reshuffle + coalescer interaction that fragments prefix locality, lowers KV hit-rate, triggers small-kernel path and L2 churn, causing p99 spike.

sylvie: thanks @marina :thumbsup: if rollback fixes it we'll add the replay guard and a canary for reshuffle on staging before any more rollouts.
